question.text: At the time of normal retirement from NPS Tier 1 at age 60, what is the maximum percentage of the accumulated corpus that can be withdrawn as a tax-free lump sum?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series X-B, at the time of exit from NPS at age 60, an NPS Tier 1 subscriber can withdraw a maximum of 60% of the accumulated corpus as a lump sum and that lump sum is tax-free under Section 10(12A). This is what makes 60% the correct answer for the maximum tax-free lump-sum percentage. The Trap: 40% is the number candidates remember as the "other portion" of the corpus, but it does not represent the tax-free lump sum, and 80% is the annuitisation figure that applies in the premature-exit case. Candidates who mix up these three percentages will pick the wrong option. Note: The exit and annuitisation requirement for the remaining corpus differs by subscriber type under current rules - for example, non-government subscribers must annuitise at least 20% at retirement while government subscribers mandatorily annuitise 40% - so do not state a single blanket annuity percentage without checking the subscriber category.
